title: Seqlen gain-driven bucket merger with KV-pressure aware thresholds
author: Maya Singh
body: Summary: Implements a new bucket-merger heuristic that decides when to merge adjacent sequence-length buckets based on expected padding gain (token savings) vs kernel cost delta and current KV-cache pressure. The core idea is: only merge buckets when the estimated net token-cost gain exceeds a threshold that adapts to runtime signals (KV hit-rate, active KV window size) and kernel cost models (per-model cost table). Motivation: previous bucketing approaches used static width/thresholds and often either over-merged (causing expensive kernel runs for long sequences) or under-merged (causing high padding waste). This PR introduces a small, runtime-safe decision function that reduces padding while avoiding detrimental kernel choice switches on the critical path.
commits: a1c3d9b: initial C++/Python hybrid implementation of gain estimator and merger
b4d5e6f: add kernel-cost lookup table and integration into batch composer
c7f8a90: expose KV pressure signal from cache manager + unit tests
d1e2f3a: tune gain-threshold defaults and add microbench harness
e4f5g6h: linting, docs and runbook for rollout
f7g8h9i: fix race in scheduler when merging live slots (hotfix requested in review)
description_details: Design notes: (1) Gain estimator computes expected padding tokens saved when two adjacent buckets are merged, factoring in the observed seqlen distribution within each bucket and the target kernel's cost function. (2) Kernel cost table is precomputed per-model/profile (latency/cost per token for common length ranges). (3) KV-pressure is a scalar in [0,1] representing recent KV cache utilization/hit-rate and active window occupancy; higher pressure raises the merge threshold to avoid expanding KV working sets. (4) Decision function: merge if (expected_padding_tokens * kernel_cost_delta) >= adaptive_threshold(KV_pressure, traffic_variance). Implementation: C++ core inside bucket_merger with a thin Python orchestration layer for tests and console hooks. Safety: merges are enacted only at scheduling quiescence points or via slot handoff to prevent races. Rollout: feature flag controlled, default off; staged enable on dedicated clusters with canary traffic.
benchmarks_summary: Microbench results (internal bench runner): mixed-seqlen traffic (30% short <32, 50% medium 32-256, 20% long >256) on A100 instance: padding tokens reduced by 22% median, end-to-end tokens/sec improved by 6-9% depending on model; P99 latency unchanged (+/- 2%) in experiments with conservative thresholds. On heavy KV-pressure synthetic runs, merge frequency dropped automatically and worst-case latency avoided.
testing: Unit tests added for estimator math, integration tests for scheduler interactions, bench harness added that reproduces the two-bucket merge latency regression case we saw in ENG-9876. Local CI caught a race when a live slot was merged; fixed by deferring commit until slot handoff completes. Stress tests run for 48 hours on staging with no memory regressions.
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Please add metrics exposables for 'bucket_merge_attempts' and 'bucket_merge_successes' so we can monitor behavior in prod. Reason: need observability for thresholds.
Maya Singh (author): Added metrics and dashboard in docs; counters are incremental and emitted per-merge-decision path.
Linnea Karlsson: Concern about scheduler race when merging while prefetch is populating KV window; suggest gating merges on prefill state.
Maya Singh (author): Implemented quiescence guard and added unit test 'merge_during_prefill' to assert no slot corruption. Reference commit f7g8h9i.
Diego Rivera: CI bench initially failed with timeout on bench-suite; rerun after reducing bench payload and it passed. Approving the approach; recommend conservative default thresholds for GA.
QA-Bot: regression-tests passed. Note: one flaky bench observed in nightly; flagged for follow-up (ticket ENG-10012).
merge_summary: Merged to main using squash. Merge commit includes tuned defaults, docs, and runbook. Rollout gated by feature flag 'seqlen_gain_merger' and enabled on dedicated clusters initially.
release_notes:
- Add adaptive seqlen bucket merger that reduces padding and improves tokens/sec for mixed-length traffic.
- Behavior adapts to KV cache pressure to avoid degrading tail latency.
- Feature gated and rolled out to dedicated clusters behind flag.
- Monitoring: bucket_merge_attempts, bucket_merge_successes, bucket_merge_rejects (KV pressure).
deployment_plan: Stage 1: disable by default; smoke on internal dedicated clusters. Stage 2 (canary): enable on 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor metrics. Stage 3: increase to 25% then 100% if stable. Rollback: flip feature flag off to stop new merges; existing merged batch behavior is safe and will naturally stop as slots drain.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in kernel switching; further follow-ups planned to add model-specific learning of thresholds and an offline trainer to propose per-customer defaults (ENG-10012).
